A General Direct Aldehyde C−H Alkylation via TBADT-Nickel
Synergistic Catalysis
Zhimin Hu,<sup>†</sup> Ji-Wei Sang,<sup>†</sup> Shize Xie,<sup>†</sup> Yujia Song,<sup>†</sup> Qiuhao Li, Bing Wang, Zheng-Yang Xu, Yu Zhang,
Runhui Liu,* Wei-Dong Zhang,* and Jinxin Wang*
ABSTRACT: Herein, we present a nickel/tetrabutylammonium decatungstate (TBADT)-catalvzed protocol for general C-H
alkylation of aldehydes, enabling the eficient synthesis of aliphatic ketones through ligand-controlled cross-coupling. This mild and
cost-efective methodology demonstrates broad substrate compatibility with various commercially available aldehydes and both
activated and unactivated alkyl bromides, delivering target products in high yields. Notably, the practical utility of this catalytic
system has been highlighted through a concise two-step synthesis of the commercially valuable musk odorant Aurelione from readily
available starting materials.

synthesize and modify bioactive natural products to discover
new drugs. Following up on our previous works,<sup>13</sup> we aimed to
develop direct aldehyde C−H functionalization reactions to
obtain various ketones eficiently and conveniently. Herein we
report a general aliphatic ketone synthesis method using
nickel/TBADT synergistic-catalyzed coupling of aldehydes
with alkyl halides via ligand control.

We next turned our attention to the scope of the aldehyde
component. As shown in Scheme 2, an assortment of aliphatic
acetones could be obtained in good to excellent yields with a
broad range of aldehydes. Aliphatic aldehydes including linear,
branched-chain, and cyclic primary, secondary, and even
tertiary aldehydes were efective coupling partners (C27−
C31 and C75−C77, C82−C84 in the Supporting Information,
47%−94% yield). Moreover, aliphatic aldehydes containing N-
Boc-piperidine, phthalimide, isopentyl, tertiary alcohols, and
furan were also coupled with high levels of eficiency (C32 and
C78−C81 in the Supporting Information, 61%−98% yield).

unsaturated ketones (C33−C35 and C93−C95 in the
Supporting Information, 59%−87% yield) in moderate to
excellent yields. This achievement is particularly significant
given the inherent challenges in suppressing competing Giese
addition pathways, a critical concern arising from the inherent
electrophilicity of both the enal substrates and the resultant
enone products. Lastly, aromatic aldehydes were found to
couple with alkyl halides proficiently, despite the diminished
hydridic nature of these C−H bonds. With the exception of
unsubstituted benzaldehydes (C36 and C85 in the Supporting
Information, 82% and 94% yield), electron-donating groups
such as alkoxy and methyl were eligible substituents on the
aromatic ring (C37−C39 and C88−C89 in the Supporting
Information, 32%−93% yields). Electron-withdrawing groups,
including common substituents such as trifluoromethyl, acetyl,
and nitro groups, could be coupled with this method (C40−
C41 and C86−C87 in the Supporting Information, 39%−62%
yields). With respect to heteroaromatic coupling partners, we
found that a range of substituted heteroaryl aldehydes are also
efective substrates (C42 and C90−C92 in the Supporting
Information, 85%, 86%, 63%, and 46% yield, respectively).
Perhaps more important was the finding that aldehydes from
natural products or drugs can be successfully employed to
generate ketones (C43−C47, 33%−74% yield). We believe
that these results demonstrate the first broadly general
approach to access aliphatic ketones from aldehydes and
alkyl halides.
To highlight a potential application to valuable molecules,
we accomplished a two-step synthesis of Aurelione, a well-
established musk odorant.<sup>17</sup> As shown in Scheme 3, 10-
undecenal A22 and 7-bromo-1-heptene B29 were successfully
combined using our aldehyde coupling protocol to forge
ketone C52 in a good yield (60%). Exposure of the
aforementioned octadeca-1,17-dien-8-one to the Grubbs
catalyst (II) in dichloromethane under reflux resulted in the
formation of Aurelione in 83% yield.
In summary, we have developed the first photoinduced
nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling protocol enabling direct
conjugation of aldehydes with diverse alkyl halides. This
sustainable methodology features operationally simple and safe
procedures conducted under environmentally benign con-
ditions, demonstrating excellent functional group compatibility
while eliminating the reliance on precious metal catalysts. The
synthetic utility of this strategy has been demonstrated through
an eficient two-step synthesis of the commercially valuable
musk fragrance Aurelione from readily available starting
materials. This catalytic paradigm not only establishes a
practical platform for sustainable aliphatic ketone synthesis but
also significantly expands accessible chemical space for
medicinal chemistry exploration while addressing critical
challenges in an environmentally conscious synthetic design.

enone products. Lastly, aromatic aldehydes were found to
couple with alkyl halides proficiently, despite the diminished
hydridic nature of these C−H bonds. With the exception of
unsubstituted benzaldehydes (C36 and C85 in the Supporting
Information, 82% and 94% yield), electron-donating groups
such as alkoxy and methyl were eligible substituents on the
aromatic ring (C37−C39 and C88−C89 in the Supporting
Information, 32%−93% yields). Electron-withdrawing groups,
including common substituents such as trifluoromethyl, acetyl,
and nitro groups, could be coupled with this method (C40−
C41 and C86−C87 in the Supporting Information, 39%−62%
yields). With respect to heteroaromatic coupling partners, we
found that a range of substituted heteroaryl aldehydes are also
efective substrates (C42 and C90−C92 in the Supporting
Information, 85%, 86%, 63%, and 46% yield, respectively).
Perhaps more important was the finding that aldehydes from
natural products or drugs can be successfully employed to
generate ketones (C43−C47, 33%−74% yield). We believe
that these results demonstrate the first broadly general
approach to access aliphatic ketones from aldehydes and
alkyl halides.
To highlight a potential application to valuable molecules,
we accomplished a two-step synthesis of Aurelione, a well-
established musk odorant.<sup>17</sup> As shown in Scheme 3, 10-
undecenal A22 and 7-bromo-1-heptene B29 were successfully
combined using our aldehyde coupling protocol to forge
ketone C52 in a good yield (60%). Exposure of the
aforementioned octadeca-1,17-dien-8-one to the Grubbs
catalyst (II) in dichloromethane under reflux resulted in the
formation of Aurelione in 83% yield.
In summary, we have developed the first photoinduced
nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling protocol enabling direct
conjugation of aldehydes with diverse alkyl halides. This
sustainable methodology features operationally simple and safe
procedures conducted under environmentally benign con-
ditions, demonstrating excellent functional group compatibility
while eliminating the reliance on precious metal catalysts. The
synthetic utility of this strategy has been demonstrated through
an eficient two-step synthesis of the commercially valuable
musk fragrance Aurelione from readily available starting
materials. This catalytic paradigm not only establishes a
practical platform for sustainable aliphatic ketone synthesis but
also significantly expands accessible chemical space for
medicinal chemistry exploration while addressing critical
challenges in an environmentally conscious synthetic design.
